title: Intermittent fasting vs. calorie restriction: which actually ...
snippet: Sep 7, 2026 · How 16:8 time-restricted eating compares For the most popular form of fasting, the daily 16:8 eating window, the picture is different. A 2023 meta-analysis in Nutrients of seven randomized trials with 458 participants found that time-restricted eating combined with a calorie deficit produced 2.11 kg more weight loss than calorie restriction alone.

title: Intermittent Fasting vs Calorie Restriction: Trials - Calorilator
snippet: Sep 20, 2026 · Trials mostly find that intermittent fasting and ordinary daily calorie restriction lead to similar weight loss. Of three head-to-head trials, two found similar results and one found modestly more loss with a fasting pattern. Reviews add that the evidence is short-term and often low certainty.

title: Intermittent fasting produces equivalent weight loss to ...
snippet: 3 days ago · A new trial shows intermittent fasting produces weight loss equivalent to calorie restriction whilst reducing the psychological burden of constant dietary monitoring. The finding suggests adherence, not metabolism, may be the key to sustained weight management.

title: Effect of Intermittent Fasting on Weight Loss in Overweight ...
snippet: Sep 15, 2026 · All the included studies demonstrated statistically significant reductions in body weight resulting from intermittent fasting interventions over durations ranging from 3 to 50 weeks. However, several trials exhibited comparable effectiveness between intermittent fasting and continuous calorie restriction.

title: Intermittent Fasting for Weight Loss: What Research Shows
snippet: Sep 14, 2026 · Alternate-day fasting has been tested head-to-head against daily calorie restriction over a full year (Trepanowski et al., 2017, JAMA Internal Medicine). Weight loss was essentially identical, roughly 6% of body weight in both groups, and the fasting group had a higher dropout rate.

title: Review Finds Intermittent Fasting Matches Calorie Cutting on ...
snippet: 1 day ago · A Frontiers in Nutrition review of 76 references reports that intermittent fasting produces weight and HbA1c changes comparable to continuous calorie restriction, with adherence differing sharply between protocols. The paper's four proposed timing-specific mechanisms rest largely on rodent studies the authors say human trials have yet to validate.
